lessons.title: Dire l’heure et organiser sa journée
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Time and schedules: Use es la una but son las dos, tres and so on.
lessons.objective: Dites l’heure avec il est, puis indiquez à quelle heure commencent et finissent les activités de la journée.
lessons.foundationTie: Builds on Core 7–9 destinations, questions and clock-time vocabulary.
lessons.focus: Il est + heure; à + heure for schedules; du matin / de l’après-midi

grammar.explanation: To tell time in French use il est, including il est une heure and il est huit heures. The hour noun changes number, but the verb stays singular: never say ils sont huit heures. For a scheduled event use à: Le cours commence à neuf heures. Ask À quelle heure ? for a precise time. Du matin and de l’après-midi disambiguate the part of the day.

model.eight: Il est huit heures du matin.
model.schedule: Le cours commence à neuf heures.
model.question: À quelle heure arrives-tu à la maison ?

grammar.caution: Unlike Spanish es la una / son las dos, French keeps il est for every clock hour.

lessons.scene: Deux camarades comparent leur emploi du temps avant la journée de cours.
dialogue: Il est huit heures du matin.|It is eight in the morning.
Le cours commence à neuf heures.|Class starts at nine.
Le déjeuner est à une heure.|Lunch is at one.
J’étudie à trois heures de l’après-midi.|I study at three in the afternoon.
La bibliothèque ferme à six heures.|The library closes at six.
À quelle heure arrives-tu à la maison ?|What time do you arrive home?
lessons.speaking: Plan a class day with a classmate. Ask what time they arrive home, tell them it is eight in the morning, then say when class, lunch, study and the library closing happen. Confirm one time by repeating it. Use il est to tell time and à for scheduled events.

words.note: Cours is a class session; salle de classe is the classroom.
Est is the third-person singular of être; the impersonal time expression is il est.
La is a feminine article or object pronoun; l’ is used before a vowel.
Sont means 'are' for plural subjects, but French clock time uses il est.
Les is a plural article or object pronoun, regardless of noun gender.

lessons.title: Dire ce qu’on aime
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Gustar: one thing or many: With gustar, the liked thing controls the verb: me gusta el libro; me gustan los libros.
lessons.objective: Exprimez vos goûts avec aimer au présent et distinguez j’aime, nous aimons, ils aiment et la négation.
lessons.foundationTie: Reuses familiar books, music and classmates while expanding present-tense verb forms from Core 1–6.
lessons.focus: Aimer + noun or infinitive; French subject agreement and ne…pas

grammar.explanation: French aimer uses the person who likes as its subject: j’aime, tu aimes, il/elle aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment. Unlike Spanish gustar, the number of liked things does not control the verb. Use aimer + definite article for a general interest (j’aime la musique) and aimer + infinitive for an activity (nous aimons étudier). Negation surrounds the conjugated verb: Luis n’aime pas le café.
grammar.caution: J’aime les livres remains j’aime even though livres is plural. Avoid copying Spanish me gusta / me gustan agreement into French.

lessons.scene: Des amis comparent leurs livres et leur musique préférée après les cours.
dialogue: Ana aime les livres.|Ana likes books.
Nous aimons étudier ensemble.|We like studying together.
Luis n’aime pas le café.|Luis does not like coffee.
Tu aimes ces chansons ?|Do you like these songs?
Oui, j’aime écouter de la musique à la maison.|Yes, I like listening to music at home.
lessons.speaking: Talk with a classmate about books, music and coffee. Ask whether they like these songs, state what you like, mention Ana and Luis, and say what you like doing together. Change roles and use at least one negative sentence. Keep the subject agreement with the person who likes.

words.note: Me is an object/reflexive pronoun; a French 'I like' sentence begins j’aime, not me aime.
Te is an object/reflexive pronoun; 'you like' is tu aimes.
Choose a preposition by location and meaning; these are not interchangeable translations.
Non answers no; ne…pas negates a verb and contracts to n’ before a vowel.

words.fr: Oui, j’aime écouter de la musique à la maison.
words.en: Yes, I like listening to music at home.

lessons.title: Vouloir et les projets du samedi
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Querer: wants: Querer changes e to ie in quiero, quieres, quiere and quieren; nosotros queremos keeps e.
lessons.objective: Dites ce que vous voulez faire avec vouloir au présent, suivi d’un infinitif, et comparez je veux, nous voulons et ils veulent.
lessons.foundationTie: Builds on Core 7 plans with aller and Core 11 infinitive activities; keeps familiar family and study contexts.
lessons.focus: Vouloir present tense + infinitive; polite choice with je voudrais

grammar.explanation: French vouloir is irregular: je veux, tu veux, il/elle veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils/elles veulent. Place an infinitive after it to express an intended action: Je veux visiter ma famille. Nous voulons manger ensemble. French does not follow the Spanish e-to-ie stem-change rule; learn the French forms as a separate pattern. Je voudrais is a softer, more polite request, but this lesson practices the present tense.

model.Ana: Ana veut se reposer à la maison.
model.they: Mes amis veulent aller au parc.

grammar.caution: The subject controls the verb: nous voulons, not nous veulent. Before an action use vouloir + infinitive without de.

lessons.scene: Le vendredi soir, des amis décident comment passer leur samedi.
dialogue: Je veux rendre visite à ma famille.|I want to visit my family.
Ana veut se reposer à la maison.|Ana wants to rest at home.
Nous voulons manger ensemble.|We want to eat together.
Luis veut acheter un livre.|Luis wants to buy a book.
Mes amis veulent aller au parc.|My friends want to go to the park.
Tu veux étudier avant de sortir ?|Do you want to study before going out?
lessons.speaking: Plan Saturday with a friend. Say you want to visit family, report Ana’s and Luis’s plans, propose eating together, and ask if the friend wants to study before going out. Repeat the agreed plan. Use veux, veut, voulons and veulent with infinitives.

words.note: The English source gloss is broad; choose à, dans or sur by context.
Mon/ma agrees with the possessed noun, with mon also before some feminine vowel-initial nouns.
De can mean of/from, but vouloir + infinitive does not take de.
